This appeal having been heard and reserved for judgment,
coming on for pronouncement this day, this Court pronounced the following :
JUDGMENT

The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 challenging the validity of the award dated 11.10.2002 passed by the VIIth Additional District Judge, Indore in Reference Case No. 81/1997 whereby the reference has been answered in negative against them and compensation award by Land Acquisition Officer has been upheld.

The facts of the case in short are as under:
1.

Vide memo No. 6287 dated 21.12.1994 the Executive Engineer (Bridge), Indore sent a request for acquisition of land bearing survey No. 235, 236, 237 and 268 total area 0.446 hectares of private land for construction of over bridge near Rajkumar Mill.

The Commissioner, District-Indore took permission from the Secretary,
Government of Madhya Pradesh for invoking the provisions of Section 4 and Section 17(1) of the Land Acquisition Act ("LA Act" for short) which is an urgency clause.

Thereafter, a gazette notification No. 103-LA/195 dated 16.02.1995 was printed in the Gazette Notification on 31.03.1995 and further duly published in daily newspapers on 12.03.1995 and on 08.03.1995 and also affixed at public places.

Thereafter,
notification under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act was - : 3 :-
issued on 10.04.1995.
All the landowners submitted their claims before the Land Acquisition Officer.

Vide award dated 24.11.1995, the Land Acquisition Officer passed an award of Rs.
91,91,543/- in respect of 16 land owners including late Gangadhar (since dead and represented through legal heirs ).
2.
Being dissatisfied with the aforesaid award, the present appellant sought a reference under section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act for the purpose of enhancement of compensation.
The reference was sent to the District Court, Indore which was registered as LA case No. 81/1997.
Apart from this appellant, one more land owner Hemchand sought reference which was registered as case No. 82/1997 (dismissed by an award dated 31.01.2001).

sentences.text: According to the appellant, the land admeasuring 91 sq.mts. and the shop constructed thereupon belonging to him and the land Acquisition Officer assessed market value @ 100 per sq.mtr. and calculated compensation of Rs.96,640/- which is on the lower side.
The Land Acquisition Officer further calculated to Rs.95,240/- under the head of construction and accordingly awarded total amount of compensation of Rs.1,92,080/-.
The Land Acquisition Officer also granted benefits of solatium of Rs.57,624/- and interest of Rs.13,577/- thus total compensation of Rs.2,63,281/- was awarded to the appellant.
The appellant before the Reference Court argued that the Land Acquisition Officer valued the land on a lower side.
The said land is liable to be valued @ Rs.1300 per sq.ft. looking at its commercial value.

According to the appellant, the respondent took possession of the - : 4 :-
area admeasuring 101 sq.ft and calculated the compensation of Rs.90/- per sq.ft.
It is further submitted that the land is situated in the heart of the city near Race Course Road where the market rate of the land is on the very higher side.
4. In support of the contention, the appellant exhibited a valuation report of an acquired property prepared by an Architecture & Government Valuer Shri Kiran P. Shindey.
According to him, the value of the land should be Rs.12,00,986/- and the value built up area should be Rs.1,52,185/-.
According to him, total value of the land comes to Rs.14,65,000/- for the purpose of the compensation.
The appellant has also got exhibited letter dated 12.04.1998 (Exhibit-P/2), Executive Engineer, Municipal Corporation, Indore for allotment of shop No. 37, Vallabh Nagar for Rs.5/- per sq.ft.

The appellant examined himself as P.W.-1, Kiran P. Shindey as P.W.2, Dattatrey, P.W.-3,
Gandhadhar P.W.-4 and in defence Government examined Ramnath Mishra, S.D.O., P.W.D.
According to him, Vallabh Nagar is 200 meters away from the acquired land.

5. After examining the entire material that came on record and the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer, the learned Additional District Judge has discarded exhibit P/1, the report submitted by the valuer on the ground that this report was prepared on 01.05.2000 after five years from the issuance of notification and witnesses P.W.-2 and 3 did not inspect the land in the year 1995.

So far as the statement of P-3 Dattatrey is concerned, who was given a piece of land on lease @
Rs.181/- per sq.ft. with rent @ of Rs.5/- per sq.ft.

the said land is situated - : 5 :-
200 ft. inside the park road.
The Reference Court has discarded the aforesaid evidence that notification under Section 4 was published dated 13.03.1995 and the shop was allotted after two and half years on 03.12.1997.

Since the appellant has not produced any registered sale deed executed during the relevant years, therefore, in absence of said evidence, the learned Reference Court has held that no case for enhancement of compensation and accordingly vide award dated 11.10.2002 dismissed the reference case.
Hence, this appeal before this Court.

sentences.text: Shri V.K. Jain, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant submitted that the acquired and shop were situated in the heart of the city that too in a commercial area of Indore having high commercial value, therefore, the compensation paid @ Rs.100/- is on a very lower side.
The report submitted by the certified valuer ought to have been accepted by the Reference Court.
Although, the report was prepared after five years but no spot inspection was required in the year 1995.
The learned Reference Court has wrongly discarded exhibit-P/2 and P/3 and the statement of P.W.-3, the distance between the land given on lease in the same locality.
The acquired land is only 200 meters away from Vallabh Nagar which is a residential area.

In view of the above submissions,
learned senior counsel prayed for enhancement of the compensation.

7. Learned Government Advocate argued in support of the impugned award by submitting that when the sale-deeds are not available of nearby properties executed in the relevant years, the - : 6 :-
Land Acquisition Officer has rightly obtained guidelines from the Registrar (Stamp)
and
as per guidelines of 1994-95 and 1995-96, the value of the land in Vallabh Nagar was Rs.180/- per sq.ft. and Rs.200/- per sq.ft. respectively.
Therefore, compensation @ Rs.100/- per sq.ft. is not liable to be entertained.

8. It is further submitted by the learned Government Advocate that the Reference Case filed by the land owner Shri Hemchand has also been dismissed by the Reference Court in which also compensation was awarded @ Rs.100/- per sq.ft.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the record.
9. Undisputed facts are that vide letter dated 21.12.1994, the Executive Engineer, PWD requested the Government to acquire land for the construction of an over bridge in the area of Rajkumar Mill.

The State Government granted permission to invoke the urgency clause under Section 17(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, therefore, the composite notification under Section 4 read with Section 17(1) was issued on 16.02.1995 and published in the Gazette Notification on 31.03.1995.

Therefore,
as per the market guidelines of the year 1994-95 for Vallabh Nagar Area, the value of the land @
Rs.100/- per sq.ft. has been taken into consideration by the Land Acquisition Officer in the absence of the sale deeds of the nearby areas.
10. The appellant has not produced any sale deed executed in the year 1994-95 in respect of the sale of the land of nearby areas .

Not only the appellant, but 16 land owners had also failed - : 7 :-
to produce any sale-deed before the Land Acquisition Officer.

Therefore, a second alternate option which was available before the Land Acquisition Officer is to assess the market value of the land on the basis of the guidelines issued by the Registrar of stamps, District-Indore for the year 1994-95 and 1995-96.

4 situated near Vallabh Nagar where in the year 1994-95, the value of the land was Rs.100/- per sq.ft. and for the year 1995-96, the value of the land was Rs.200/- per sq.ft.

sentences.text: The land allotted by the Indore Municipal Corporation to the Shri Dattatrey is in park road area where the market rate as per guidelines was Rs.250/- per sq.ft. in the year 1994-95 and Rs.275/- per sq.ft. in the year 1995-96.
Admittedly the acquired land is situated in a residential as well as in commercial area both and was not available to be used for agricultural purposes.
Near Vallabh Nagar, there is a Railway Station, G.S.I.T.S. College, Nehru Park, Telephone Exchange etc.
therefore, the land was having residential as well as commercial value.
Since the acquired area is very small, and the shop was constructed thereon.
The notification was published on 31.03.1995 i.e. the last day of the guidelines issued for the year 1994-95 and thereafter, for the year 1995-96, it has been doubled i.e. R.200/- per sq.ft.

therefore in my considered opinion, the appellant would be entitled to compensation by taking the market value of the least @ Rs.125/- per sq.ft. looking to the location and commercial value of the land.
Hence, the appeal is partly allowed.

11. The Executing Court shall calculate the amount of compensation @ Rs.125/- per sq.ft. and accordingly, calculate the - : 8 :-
interest as well as consolation.
There shall be no enhancement in respect of the cost of construction of the shop.
12. The first appeal stands partly allowed and disposed of to the extent indicated above.
No order as to cost and record be sent back.
